newsitem.title: INDIA: ING Barings lowers India TELCO earnings.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings lowers India TELCO earnings.

text.p: Securities firm ING Barings said on Wednesday it lowered its 1996/97 (April-March) and 1997/98 earnings estimates for Indian truckmaker TELCO.

"In line with our view of recessionary trends in the economy in general and a slowdown in the automobile sector in particular, we are downgrading our numbers on TELCO," ING Barings said in a note to investors.
It said its maintained its underweight recommendation on the stock.
The securities firm said it revised TELCO's 1996/97 sales volumes to 199,973 units from 210,852. Net profit for the year was lowered to 5,860 million rupees from a previous estimate of 6,596 million.

ING Barings said sales volumes would see a drop in 1997/98, and revised its estimate to 179,471 units from the previous 225,082 units. Net profit for the year was forecast sharply lower at 2,498 million against a previous 6,758 million.

"We now expect TELCO's volumes to grow by a lower 10 percent y-o-y in 1996/97 (against 16 percent estimated earlier) and to fall by 10 percent y-o-y in 1997/98 (against 7 percent growth projected earlier)," the note said.
"Given the very high sensitivity of earnings to volumes, we expect a 59 percent y-o-y slump in earnings in 1997/98."

ING Barings said dealers had indicated a pile up of light commercial vehicle (LCV) inventories, off the shelf availability at no premium on medium and heavy commercial vehicles and a reduced premium on the Sumo model.

"Cargo handlers indicate increased vehicle downtime and stagnant freight rates even during the supposedly busy season. Finance companies indicate slack demand even with easy availability and slightly lower interest rates, while ancillaries are talking of impending production cuts," the note said.
